reason: E2 directly supports the concept that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility in RHEAs, but it does not involve NbMoTaW or Ti addition. No cited evidence supports the specific claim that Ti addition and aging will produce this microstructure in NbMoTaW, nor that it will preserve high-temperature strength or improve irradiation tolerance. E4 suggests compositional complexity may increase He irradiation tolerance but does not address the proposed mechanism or microstructure. E1 and E3 provide only general background.
premises: Adding Ti and aging NbMoTaW will produce discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix
This 'inverted' BCC+B2 microstructure enhances room-temperature ductility in RHEAs
The B2 precipitates will not significantly reduce high-temperature strength up to 1600°C
Heterogeneous microstructure with precipitates improves irradiation tolerance by acting as defect sinks
The specific Ti content (~5 at%) and aging (~900°C) are optimal for this microstructure
